_link.title: I can describe the role of the somatic nervous system and the neural pathways it contains

toLevel2.stem: The somatic nervous system is a division of which part of the nervous system?
distractors: The central nervous system
The autonomic nervous system
The sympathetic nervous system

toLevel2.stem: What is the primary role of the somatic nervous system?
toLevel2.answer: Transmitting messages for voluntary motor movement
distractors: Regulating involuntary organ function automatically
Controlling heart rate and digestive system activity
Processing sensory information within the brain only

toLevel2.stem: Sensory (afferent) neural pathways in the somatic nervous system carry messages in which direction?
distractors: Away from the CNS
Between two muscles
Within the brain only

toLevel2.stem: Motor (efferent) neural pathways in the somatic nervous system carry messages from the CNS to which structures?
distractors: Internal organs only
Smooth muscle tissue
Glands and blood vessels

toLevel2.stem: Which types of neurons make up the neural pathways of the somatic nervous system?
distractors: Motor neurons and interneurons only
Interneurons and sensory neurons only
Only motor neurons for all its pathways

toLevel2.stem: The somatic nervous system contains both sensory (afferent) and motor (efferent) neural pathways.
distractors: False

toLevel2.stem: The somatic nervous system is responsible for controlling involuntary functions such as heart rate and digestion.
distractors: True

toLevel2.stem: The somatic nervous system is a division of the {{blank:1}} that transmits neural messages related to voluntary motor movement.

distractors: CNS

toLevel3.stem: Why does the somatic nervous system need both sensory and motor neural pathways?
toLevel3.answer: Sensory pathways detect stimuli; motor pathways produce responses
distractors: Both pathways carry the same type of information to muscles
Sensory pathways control organs; motor pathways control glands
Motor pathways detect stimuli; sensory pathways produce actions

toLevel3.stem: How does the somatic nervous system differ from the autonomic nervous system?
toLevel3.answer: The SNS controls voluntary movement; the ANS controls involuntary functions
distractors: The SNS controls involuntary functions; the ANS controls voluntary actions
The SNS is part of the CNS; the ANS is part of the peripheral system
The SNS only contains motor neurons; the ANS only contains interneurons

toLevel3.stem: What does the term 'afferent' mean in the context of neural pathways?
distractors: Carrying messages away from the CNS
Carrying messages between two neurons
Carrying messages within the brain only

toLevel3.stem: Why is the somatic nervous system described as being involved in the spinal reflex?
toLevel3.answer: Its sensory and motor neurons form part of the reflex arc
distractors: The spinal reflex is a voluntary response controlled by the SNS
The somatic nervous system processes reflexes in the brain only
The autonomic nervous system has no role in any reflexive action

toLevel3.stem: What does the term 'efferent' mean in the context of neural pathways?
toLevel3.answer: Carrying messages away from the CNS
distractors: Carrying messages toward the CNS
Carrying messages between two neurons
Carrying messages within the spinal cord

toLevel3.stem: Why do motor neurons in the somatic nervous system specifically target skeletal muscles rather than organs?
distractors: Organs do not contain any nerve endings
Skeletal muscles are the only body tissue
Organs are controlled by the somatic system

toLevel3.stem: The somatic nervous system is involved in the spinal reflex because its sensory and motor neurons form part of the reflex arc.
distractors: False

toLevel3.stem: The somatic nervous system differs from the autonomic nervous system because the SNS controls {{blank:1}} movement while the ANS controls involuntary functions.

distractors: involuntary
unconscious

toLevel3.stem: Afferent pathways carry messages {{blank:1}} the CNS, while efferent pathways carry messages {{blank:2}} the CNS.

distractors: away from
within

toLevel3.stem: The somatic nervous system is involved in the spinal reflex because its {{blank:1}} and motor neurons form part of the reflex arc.

distractors: autonomic

toLevel4.stem: Chloe reaches out to catch a ball thrown toward her. Which description correctly applies the somatic nervous system to this action?
toLevel4.answer: Sensory neurons carry visual information to the CNS; motor neurons carry commands to arm muscles
distractors: Motor neurons carry visual information to the CNS; sensory neurons carry commands to arm muscles
Interneurons carry visual information directly to the skeletal muscles in her arm for the response
The autonomic nervous system carries all messages needed for this voluntary catching movement

toLevel4.stem: Jake accidentally touches a hot stove and his hand jerks away. Which neural pathway in the somatic nervous system initiated this response?
toLevel4.answer: Sensory neurons carried the pain signal toward the CNS
distractors: Motor neurons carried the pain signal toward the CNS
Interneurons carried the pain signal to skeletal muscles
Autonomic neurons carried the pain signal to the spinal cord

toLevel4.stem: A physiotherapist asks Mia to lift her right arm above her head. Which neural pathway completes the final stage of this voluntary movement?
toLevel4.answer: Motor neurons carry the command from the CNS to arm muscles
distractors: Sensory neurons carry the command from the CNS to the arm
Interneurons carry the command directly to the arm muscles
Autonomic neurons carry the command to the arm's smooth muscle

toLevel4.stem: Tom is writing an exam answer about a person kicking a football. He needs to identify which division of the nervous system is responsible. Which is correct?
distractors: The autonomic nervous system
The sympathetic nervous system
The parasympathetic nervous system

toLevel4.stem: A doctor tests a patient's knee-jerk reflex. Which component of the somatic nervous system detects the tap on the knee?
toLevel4.answer: Sensory neurons in the afferent pathway
distractors: Motor neurons in the efferent pathway only
Interneurons located in the skeletal muscles
Autonomic neurons in the sympathetic division

toLevel4.stem: Priya feels the texture of a fabric with her fingertips. Which somatic nervous system pathway is responsible for transmitting this sensory information?
toLevel4.answer: The sensory (afferent) pathway toward the CNS
distractors: The motor (efferent) pathway away from the CNS
The autonomic pathway to the internal organs only
The sympathetic pathway for arousal and alertness

toLevel4.stem: A student writes: 'The somatic nervous system only contains motor neurons.' How should this statement be corrected?
toLevel4.answer: It also contains sensory neurons in afferent pathways
distractors: The statement is correct and no correction is needed
It only contains interneurons, not motor neurons at all
It contains autonomic neurons rather than motor neurons

toLevel4.stem: When Chloe catches a ball, {{blank:1}} neurons carry visual information to the CNS, and {{blank:2}} neurons carry the movement command to her arm muscles.

distractors: motor
autonomic

distractors: motor

toLevel4.stem: Kicking a football is a voluntary action that involves the {{blank:1}} nervous system, which is a division of the PNS.

distractors: autonomic

toLevel5.stem: A student claims that the somatic nervous system only handles voluntary actions and plays no role in reflexes. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; somatic sensory and motor neurons are part of the reflex arc
distractors: Correct; reflexes are entirely handled by the autonomic nervous system
Correct; the spinal cord operates independently of somatic pathways
Incorrect; the somatic system handles reflexes but not voluntary actions

toLevel5.stem: A student argues that sensory neurons and motor neurons in the somatic nervous system carry messages in the same direction. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; sensory neurons go toward the CNS and motor neurons go away
distractors: Correct; both types of neurons carry messages toward the central system
Correct; both types of neurons carry messages away from the central system
Incorrect; neither type of neuron has a specific direction of transmission

toLevel5.stem: Dr Singh claims that the somatic nervous system is part of the central nervous system. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; the somatic nervous system is a division of the PNS
distractors: Correct; the somatic nervous system is located within the brain
Correct; all motor pathways are classified as part of the CNS
Incorrect; the somatic nervous system is part of the ANS only

toLevel5.stem: A student writes that the somatic nervous system sends messages to organs and glands. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; it sends messages to skeletal muscles, not organs
distractors: Correct; the somatic nervous system controls all body tissues
Correct; organs and glands are controlled by somatic pathways
Incorrect; the somatic system does not send messages at all

toLevel5.stem: Emma argues that the term 'afferent' should be replaced with 'incoming' in all textbooks for clarity. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Both terms are valid, but afferent is the standard scientific term
distractors: Correct; 'incoming' is more accurate than 'afferent' in all cases
Incorrect; 'afferent' and 'incoming' mean completely different things
Incorrect; 'afferent' actually means outgoing rather than incoming

toLevel5.stem: A student claims that because the somatic nervous system controls voluntary movement, all movements involving skeletal muscles must be voluntary. Which evaluation is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; spinal reflexes also involve skeletal muscles involuntarily
distractors: Correct; skeletal muscles are only ever activated through voluntary action
Correct; involuntary movements only ever involve smooth muscle tissue
Incorrect; the somatic nervous system does not control skeletal muscles

toLevel5.stem: Marcus argues that the autonomic nervous system could replace the somatic nervous system for voluntary actions if needed. Which evaluation is most justified?
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; the ANS controls involuntary functions, not voluntary movement
distractors: Correct; the ANS can control voluntary movement when the SNS is damaged
Correct; both divisions are interchangeable for all types of body responses
Incorrect; the ANS does not exist and cannot replace any other division

toLevel5.stem: A textbook describes the somatic nervous system as containing 'only motor pathways.' A student questions this. Which evaluation supports the student?
toLevel5.answer: The SNS also contains sensory pathways, so the textbook is incomplete
distractors: The textbook is correct because the SNS only uses motor neuron pathways
The student is wrong because sensory pathways belong to the CNS division
The textbook is correct because sensory neurons are part of the ANS only

toLevel5.stem: The claim that the somatic nervous system only handles voluntary actions is {{blank:1}} because somatic neurons are also involved in the {{blank:2}}.

distractors: correct
plausible
autonomic response
sympathetic response

toLevel5.stem: A description of the somatic nervous system that omits {{blank:1}} pathways is incomplete because the SNS contains both sensory and motor neural pathways.

distractors: autonomic
